edges.effect_quant: The observational literature consistently points toward higher later IBD risk after antibiotic exposure in infancy or toddlerhood. In a Norwegian nationwide cohort, antibiotic exposure before age 2 was associated with an adjusted odds ratio of 1.33 for later pediatric IBD, with a stronger association after more than 2 courses and for broad-spectrum agents.
edges.population: children exposed to systemic antibiotics during the first 2 years of life
edges.mechanism: Antibiotics given during a critical window of microbiome assembly may alter gut microbial diversity, immune education, and mucosal barrier homeostasis in ways that increase later susceptibility to inflammatory bowel disease. Repeated and broad-spectrum exposure may amplify that disruption.
edges.summary: The signal is directionally harmful, though entirely observational. Large register studies and pediatric IBD cohorts consistently link early-life antibiotic exposure with higher later IBD risk, especially with repeated courses or broader-spectrum antibiotics.
edges.caveats: Confounding by infection burden is a real concern, because children who receive antibiotics differ from unexposed children in ways not fully captured by administrative data. Even so, newer analyses that adjust for infection frequency still tend to show a residual association.
